subject: Post-call: Tool-calling integration patterns / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps  - tool-calling & integration patterns

Thanks again for the call earlier, Samir (and Laura)  - good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the tech workshop: 

Summary (high-level)
- Goal: Integrate Redwood inference into FinApps' decision engine for transaction classification and risk signals. You want low-latency routing for live transactions and an offline reranker for batch enrichment.
- Key integration areas we discussed: SDK setup & auth, request routing (latency vs cost), structured output / tool-calling (for deterministic actions), and embeddings + reranker for retrieval-based augmentation.

Architecture / integration notes we agreed on
- SDKs: Python + Node SDKs (we support both). You can use API keys for server-side services or OAuth/service-account flows for user-scoped access.
- Routing: We recommend a primary low-latency model for live decisions + a cheaper, higher-throughput model for batch/rerank. Smart routing rules can fallback on region/capacity.
- Tool/function calling: Define explicit tool schemas (id, input schema, output schema, timeout) so the LLM can call external actions (e.g., call_risk_api, fetch_customer_history). Prefer typed/JSON output for programmatic parsing.
- Parallel tools: For 3rd-party enrichments we discussed invoking enrichment calls in parallel and aggregating results before a final model pass. This reduces end-to-end latency but requires careful error handling.
- Error handling: Timeouts, retries, and deterministic fallbacks (e.g., cached score or default rule) are essential. Also validate tool outputs with a JSON schema and have a safe fallback path.
- Embeddings/reranker: Use high-quality embeddings for candidate retrieval, then run a reranker model (smaller, tuned) to reorder top-k. We recommend evaluating cost vs accuracy tradeoffs on a sample workload.

Action items / next steps
1) Tech workshop: Schedule a 90-min deep-dive with your engineering + our SE (Dev). We'll walk through example tool definitions, routing policies, and run a short live integration demo.
2) I'll share example tool definitions + architecture diagram (attached).
3) Dev will prep a short checklist: request/response JSON schema, auth options, expected token impact estimates for the two flows (live + rerank).

Do you have any constraints we should know about ahead of the workshop (private cloud/VPC, strict HSM/KMS requirements, or specific latency SLOs)?

Thanks  - I'll follow up with a proposed calendar invite.

 -Marissa

Hey Samir  - quick answers and a few concrete patterns you can review ahead of the workshop. I'll be the SE on the call.

Auth recommendations
- Server-to-server in a private VPC: API keys with mTLS are a pragmatic option. If you need per-user scoping or delegated access, use OAuth/service-account tokens. We support KMS/HSM integrations for key wrapping; you can store your signing key and use it to generate short-lived tokens.

SDK parity
- Node & Python parity is good for basic features. Streaming + function/tool-calling primitives are available in both SDKs. We have a couple of language-specific helpers for concurrency in Node (Promise-based patterns) and for async batching in Python.

Tool definition example (simple JSON snippet)
- We define tools as lightweight JSON metadata plus an endpoint. Example (as a text snippet below):

TOOL DEFINITION (example)
{
  "id": "call_customer_profile",
  "description": "Fetch customer profile from FinApps enrichment service",
  "input_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string"}},
    "required": ["customer_id"]
  },
  "output_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"risk_score": {"type": "number"}, "profile": {"type": "object"}}
  },
  "timeout_ms": 2000,
  "retry_policy": {"max_retries": 2, "backoff_ms": 200}
}

Patterns for parallel tools + error handling
- Orchestrator approach: invoke enrichment tools in parallel and collect results with a soft-deadline (e.g., 2s). If a tool times out, record an error tag in the enrichment result and continue with available data.
- Retry policy: short retries with exponential backoff; avoid blocking the decision path for long.
- Partial results: allow the model/final pass to operate on partial enrichments. Mark missing fields explicitly to help model reason about gaps.
- Fallback: if all enrichments fail, use a cached baseline score or a deterministic rule. Also consider running a lightweight local model as a guardrail.

Structured output validation
- Validate every tool output against the declared JSON schema. If validation fails, surface the raw output to logs and trigger a fallback. We provide a schema validator in the SDK that returns detailed diffs.

Reranker pattern
- Retrieval: produce top-N candidates via vector search (embedding similarity).
- Rerank: synchronous call to a tuned reranker model on the top-K (K=8-32 depending on latency/cost). Prefer a smaller reranker to reduce cost.
- Score aggregation: keep per-candidate metadata (source confidence, tool-enrichment flags) for explainability.

Observability / telemetry
- Trace each request across tool calls, model calls, and routing decisions. Include token counts in traces and surface cold-start or cache-hit metrics.

I'll attach an example tool-def file and a short checklist (attached to Marissa's email). Happy to walk through code snippets in the workshop.

 -Dev
